The word-boundary truncation logic and apostrophe-handling fix look correct and match the docstring's described algorithm (verified against every test case by hand, including the exact-length and long-first-word edge cases).

However, there's a real problem: the PR bumps `DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH` from 40 to 50, but the docstring still says verbatim "`max_length` defaults to `DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH`, which is 40." That line was never updated, so the code and its own docstring now directly contradict each other — exactly the kind of inconsistency the teammate asked us to avoid ("the docstrings are the source of truth").

Worse, tracing through the docstring's own truncation algorithm (greedy leading-word inclusion) against `test_default_length_for_long_titles`, the expected output `"a-practical-guide-to-migrating-legacy-billing"` is 45 characters long — it can only be produced if `DEFAULT_MAX_LENGTH` is somewhere in the range [45, 52]. With the documented value of 40, the same algorithm produces `"a-practical-guide-to-migrating-legacy"` (37 chars) instead, which doesn't match the test. So the docstring's stated default (40) and the test are mutually inconsistent no matter how the truncation logic is implemented — the PR papers over this by picking 50 out of the valid range with no justification tying it back to any spec, which reads as "whatever number makes the test green" rather than a principled fix.

Before merging, this discrepancy needs to be resolved and called out explicitly (e.g., update the docstring line to state the actual default, and note in the PR description that this is a behavior change to the public default affecting any callers relying on the implicit 40-character default) rather than silently changed. As-is, this is a real behavioral change to a public constant that's undocumented and inconsistent with the docstring, so I'd send this back rather than merge.
